message:
test(tls): read the posture off a live session, and refuse a real bad certificate

Three claims that were being carried as one, separated so that what ran and
what did not are legible at a glance.

The options are now read back with WinHttpQueryOption from a session the
product's own function configured. WinHttpSetOption can fail quietly, so
"the code calls SetOption" and "the session carries the value" are different
facts, and only the second one is evidence. The redirect policy reads back
as DISALLOW_HTTPS_TO_HTTP and not as the default that follows the redirect.
The protocol set refuses to be read back at all on this stack (error 87), so
that one is a SKIP rather than a pass -- a query that failed is not an
assertion that the protocols are right.

A certificate that does not check out is now genuinely refused: an https
server on loopback with a throwaway self-signed certificate, dialled with
the product's transport, fails with the certificate named and nothing
returned from behind it. The fixture is generated per run into a directory
beside the test executable, the server is a child process this test holds a
handle to and terminates by that handle, and both are removed after the path
is confirmed to be the one this run made. No store is touched.

What is NOT tested, and is printed as SKIP rather than left to be assumed:

  * The https -> http redirect refusal in flight. It cannot be reached from
    a self-signed fixture, because the handshake fails first -- the request
    never gets as far as a redirect. An assertion there would be green
    whether or not the policy existed, which is a pass for the wrong reason.
    Reaching it needs a certificate the machine trusts, and a test does not
    change a trust store.
  * A valid https exchange succeeding. Only refusals are exercised here, so
    a transport that refused everything would pass this file. That
    comparison waits for a real TLS endpoint, and until then https
    reachability is unverified.
